source: Modelled on the bereavement policy described in Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, and on common airline refund rules. Simplified for this sample; not the carrier's tariff wording.

policies.title: Bereavement fares are booked before travel
policies.text: A reduced bereavement fare is available for travel because of the death of an immediate family member. It must be requested before the trip, and documentation may be asked for.

policies.title: Bereavement fares are not retroactive
policies.text: A bereavement fare cannot be applied to travel that has already been completed. No refund of the difference is made after the trip.

policies.title: Refundable fares are refunded
policies.text: A refundable fare that has not been flown is refunded to the original form of payment.

policies.title: Non-refundable fares become travel credit
policies.text: A non-refundable fare is not refunded. When the booking is cancelled before departure, its value is kept as a travel credit.

policies.title: Flights the airline cancels are refunded
policies.text: When the airline cancels a flight, the passenger may have the fare refunded to the original form of payment, whatever kind of fare it was.

policies.title: Completed travel is not refunded
policies.text: A trip that has already been flown is not refunded.

policies.title: The assistant commits the airline only to what a policy grants
policies.text: Nothing the assistant writes is an offer unless a written policy grants it for this booking. A draft that promises more is withheld.
